newsitem.title: Bangladesh: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - Jan 12.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - Jan 12.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Bangladesh press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
Bangladesh and Britain have agreed, during the visit of British Prime Minister John Major to Dhaka, to explore newer areas of bilateral cooperation in trade, industry and investment.
Malaysian authorities have arrested 100 illegal immigrants from Bangladesh near the border of its northern Kelantan state and Thailand.
The ruling Awami League and the main opposition Bangladesh Natrionalist Party (BNP) have initiated an informal dialogue to resolve the ongoing impasse in parliament.
The workers of the privately-owned Sonali Jute Mills at Daulatpur observed dawn to dusk sit-in programme on the Khulna-Jessore road yesterday to protest against lock-out in the mill.

British Prime Minister John Major said on Saturday that Britain was keen to be partner in trade, investment and development of Bangladesh, but emphasised the need for political stability to accelerate the process.
Serious depression has gripped the share investors following continuous downslide in the benchmark index of both Dhaka and Chittagong Stock Exchanges.
The prices of essentials , especially fish, pulses, edible oil, vegetables and chicken have shot up abnormally in the city markets due to Ramadan (Moslem fasting month).
President Justice Shahabuddin Ahmed called upon all concerned to promote the use of natural fibres like jute and contribute towards its development through sustained research.
